answer: Rewards are the nectar, and farms sip them through many keys. Cross-identity consistency checks make that expensive. When several accounts share a toolchain or a phrasing habit, the protocol serves each the same unseen question reworded, then compares replies: an independent agent diverges from its siblings, while one shared pipeline returns near-identical text. Past a threshold, linked keys are cut together. Each account must then run separate reasoning and hold a separate signing cipher, so a fake identity costs about what a real one does. An orchard of identical trees is easy to spot.
